key_numbers.name: Revenue Growth (YoY)
key_numbers.plain_english: The percentage year-over-year rate of change in top-line net sales revenue compared to the exact same quarter last year.
key_numbers.what_it_signifies: Measures core commercial demand momentum and price realization across identical seasonal cycles, filtering out seasonal distortion.

key_numbers.name: Operating Profit (EBITDA ex-Other Income) Margin
key_numbers.plain_english: Core operating profitability from commercial goods sold before financing costs, depreciation, non-operating treasury income, and direct taxes.
key_numbers.what_it_signifies: Isolates pure operating manufacturing and distribution profitability. Shows what percentage of each rupee earned remains after direct operating expenses.

key_numbers.name: Operating Margin YoY Spread
key_numbers.plain_english: The expansion or contraction in operating profit margin percentage points across a full 12-month seasonal cycle.
key_numbers.what_it_signifies: Quantifies operational cost leverage. A negative spread indicates input commodity inflation, freight, or ad-spends expanding faster than sales realization.

key_numbers.name: Operating Expense Growth (YoY)
key_numbers.plain_english: How fast total operating expenditures (raw material costs, employee overhead, advertising, freight) increased over the past 12 months.
key_numbers.what_it_signifies: Compared directly against top-line sales growth (+10.05% vs +10.53%); when expense growth outpaces revenue growth, margins compress.

key_numbers.name: Operating Cash Flow (CFO) to EBITDA Conversion
key_numbers.plain_english: The proportion of audited annual Operating Profit (EBITDA ex-Other Income) that actually materialized as physical cash flow from operations.
key_numbers.what_it_signifies: Rigorous earnings quality test matching identical audited annual periods. A sustained shift (Mar 2025: 80.9% -> Mar 2026: 73.1%) indicates cash absorption into working capital.

key_numbers.name: Trade Receivables / Debtor Days (DSO)
key_numbers.plain_english: The average number of days required for the company to collect cash from wholesale distributors and retail accounts after delivering goods.
key_numbers.what_it_signifies: Measures distributor credit discipline. Rising debtor days indicates trade partners delaying payments; falling days indicates disciplined cash collections.

key_numbers.name: Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO)
key_numbers.plain_english: The average duration finished goods and raw materials sit in distribution warehouses before being sold.
key_numbers.what_it_signifies: Reflects working capital tied up in supply chain inventory buffers. Expansion indicates potential channel inventory buildup or raw material stockpiling.

key_numbers.name: Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC)
key_numbers.plain_english: The net operational turnover cycle funded by corporate working capital versus vendor supplier credit.
key_numbers.what_it_signifies: A negative cycle (-89.0 days) demonstrates that the company's suppliers are effectively funding its entire operating working capital.
